projects.title: Atlas · Read Any Codebase as a City
projects.description: Turns a public GitHub repository into an interactive isometric city map. Directories become districts, files become buildings as tall as the code inside them, and the handful of files that actually matter stand out as landmarks. Four agents handle one request end to end (Ingester, Parser, Layout, Annotator) on Cloudflare Pages Functions with no model in the loop, so the same repository always renders the same city and two of them can be compared.Built solo in 48 hours for the IBM Bob Hackathon (NativelyAI/lablab.ai with IBM) and placed 2nd of 503 submissions, from 1,672 teams and 5,628 participants, taking $3,000 of the $10,000 prize pool. Eight Korean outlets covered it.The judged build is permanently tagged v1.0-hackathon so it stays unambiguous: flat 2D maps, one theme, no dependency arcs at all, 78 tests. Everything since then is a continuation of it. Isometric renderer over SVG and canvas, two themes, real import resolution, and an ingester that replaced 243 API calls with a single gzipped tar stream from codeload.github.com, which dropped Hono from 16.5s to 1.1s and left theservice holding no GitHub credential. 269 tests.

projects.title: Oneline · Natural-Language Personal-Tool Generator
projects.description: Selected for the Google I/O Hackathon (Cerebral Valley × Google DeepMind, May 2026, in-person SF, application-gated). Built Oneline solo in 6.5 hours, a generator that turns a one-line request into a working tool deployed to your phone in about two minutes. Three candidates build in parallel inside Gemini Managed Agents sandboxes, a three-layer judge scores each (functionality via Playwright run in-sandbox, plus UX and design), and losing builds become lessons that improve the next one. Every model call runs on Gemini 3.5 Flash.

An intense week inside the Google I/O 2026 ecosystem in San Francisco. Thursday at the Google for Startups × Google DeepMind After Hours, hands-on with the newest generative media models. Saturday, the Cerebral Valley × Google DeepMind hackathon at SHACK15 , where I built Oneline. Most software is built for everyone, so it fits no one. The tool you need most is often the one nobody built, because the market is just you. Oneline turns a one-line request into a working tool on your phone in about two minutes. When you describe one: → Three versions build in parallel, each in its own Gemini Managed Agents sandbox → A three-layer judge scores them, running the real tool with Playwright inside the sandbox → The winner deploys to Cloud Run, with a QR to your phone Every losing version leaves a lesson that improves the next build. Every model call runs on Gemini 3.5 Flash. Built solo in 6.5 hours. Not an app builder like Lovable or V0, which ship to a market. Oneline builds one tool for one person, who uses it and throws it away. The market is one. I believe the ML engineering job market is splitting in two. On one side: full-stack AI engineers who ship products end-to-end. On the other: hyper-specialists optimizing TPUs and training $50M models. The traditional middle ground of ML engineers building feature pipelines and training scikit-learn models is disappearing. Here's what's actually happening: Path 1: The Full-Stack AI Engineer ❯❯❯❯ Understands ML fundamentals and model behavior ❯❯❯❯ Can ship an AI feature end-to-end in a week ❯❯❯❯ Owns the product surface, backend, and model integration ❯❯❯❯ Knows when to use GPT-4 vs fine-tune vs RAG ❯❯❯❯ Typical environment: Series A-C startups, mid-size companies Think: The person who can take "add AI search to our product" from concept to production without handing off between 4 teams. Path 2: The Hyper-Specialist ❯❯❯❯ TPU kernel optimization ❯❯❯❯ Distributed training infrastructure ❯❯❯❯ LLM post-training techniques ❯❯❯❯ Custom CUDA kernels for specific architectures ❯❯❯❯ Typical environment: FAANG, OpenAI, Anthropic, Databricks Think: The person who shaves 30% off training costs for models that cost $50M+ to train. Reality: There are maybe 50-100 companies globally running billion-user ML systems. AutoML/LLMs handle simpler cases Product requirements demand faster iteration Companies can't afford specialized ML teams unless at massive scale What this means for your career if you're not at a top-10 tech company: Learn to ship. Fast. Understand enough ML to make good decisions, not build from scratch Get comfortable with APIs, prompt engineering, and fine-tuning Own more of the stack If you want the specialist path: Get deep. Really deep. Target the handful of companies doing cutting-edge infrastructure Publish, contribute to open source, build credibility Expect a more competitive, narrower job market

Introducing Claude Opus 5: a thoughtful and proactive model that comes close to the frontier intelligence of Fable 5 at half the price. On several coding and knowledge work evaluations, Opus 5 is the new state-of-the-art. It’s also highly efficient—it outperforms other models for a similar or lower cost per task. According to our automated behavioral audit, Opus 5 is our most aligned model to date. It shows the lowest rates of reckless or deceptive behavior, and the strongest adherence to Claude’s Constitution. It’s available today on all paid plans and the Claude API, priced the same as Opus 4.8. It’s the default model on Claude Max, and the strongest on Claude Pro. 토스를 떠난 뒤로 링크드인에 한동안 소식을 남기지 못했네요. 그 사이 저는 우아한형제들, 배달의민족에 합류했고 어느새 8개월이 되었습니다. 짧다면 짧은 시간이지만 정말 많은 일이 있었어요. 부문 소속이던 조직이 대표 직속으로 재편되면서, 배민에서 고객경험을 하나의 지원 기능이 아니라 사업의 중요한 요소로 다루기 시작한 시점이기도 했습니다. 저는 요즘 매일 매일 새로운 시장을 배우며, 밀도 높은 경험으로 많은 시간을 채우고 있습니다. 그리고 이번에 KMAC가 주최한 AXIS(Asia eXperience & Innovation Summit)에서 CX에 대하여 발표할 기회가 있었는데요. 주제는 "CX는 비용인가, 투자인가, Profitability를 만드는 고객경험 전략"이었습니다. 발표에서 전하고 싶었던 세 가지는 이렇습니다. 1. Asset - CX는 P&L 의 비용 라인이 아니라 B/S 의 무형 자산이며 가치 자산이다. 2. Proof - CX가 중요하다는 합의를 넘어 얼마를 만들어낸다는 증명을 숫자로 해야한다. 3. Ai-Human - AI 시대일수록 휴먼 에이전트는 더 값비싼 투자가 된다. CX의 Profitability 를 표현하는건 어려운 일이지만, CX를 가치있는 자산으로 만들기 위한 고민들을 이야기 드릴 수 있는 자리였습니다. 좋은 기회의 발표였고, 앞으로도 CX에 대한 이야기들도 조금씩 나눠보겠습니다. 고민되는 분들이 있다면 언제든 연락 주세요 :) #CX #고객경험 #AXIS2026 #KMAC #CXProfitability

Yesterday I told my co-founder we have return flights to LA without a single meeting booked yet. He called me crazy. Here's why I'm not. Vihaan Shringi and I built Presonance : a model that predicts how viewers will behave with your content before you even post it. We benchmarked against trillion-dollar companies whose bread and butter this is, and blew them out of the water. But here's the thing: the best marketers have been making this exact prediction on instinct for decades. They'd know better than anyone what works and where we can be useful. Those are the conversations worth flying for. So from Thursday July 16 to Monday July 20, we're in Los Angeles, spending all five days with CMOs, marketing and advertising leads at brands, agency owners, and people building in the creative space. Show us where this breaks. If you're right, we'll have learned more in one meeting than a month of evals. And if we're right, you'll have seen it first. If that's you, comment or DM me and I'll send times. If it's someone you know, tag them. He's probably right to call me crazy. Come anyway.
